title: Bug: Multiple registration tasks
body:
Due to the error "Less than 500 bytes/sec transferred in the last 5 seconds" it is possible to create several registration tasks that will be added every second and thus consume the CPU

```
2026-02-20 16:11:21 I game: kill killer='5:scattredredeen' victim='6:delous' weapon=5 special=0
2026-02-20 16:11:21 E http: https://master1.ddnet.org/ddnet/15/register failed. libcurl error (28): Operation too slow. Less than 500 bytes/sec transferred the last 5 seconds.
2026-02-20 16:11:21 E register/6/ipv4: error sending request to master.
2026-02-20 16:11:23 E http: https://master1.ddnet.org/ddnet/15/register failed. libcurl error (28): Operation too slow. Less than 500 bytes/sec transferred in the last 5 seconds
2026-02-20 16:11:23 E register/6/ipv4: error sending request to master
2026-02-20 16:11:24 E http: https://master1.ddnet.org/ddnet/15/register failed. libcurl error (28): Operation too slow. Less than 500 bytes/sec transferred in the last 5 seconds
2026-02-20 16:11:24 E register/6/ipv4: error sending request to master
```
This is evident from the seconds in this log: 21, 23, and 24, each of these tasks waits 5 seconds!! Because of this, one thread is consumed (on my server, 4.4 Ghz).
Tasks are created using `CRegister::OnNewInfo(const char *pInfo)` and `CRegister::Update()`.

I think it's better to create a variable that indicates whether a task is already running, so as not to kill the previous task.

title: Server records duplicated messages to server demos when sending messages to all clients
body:
1. Start recording a server demo with 2 clients on a server.
2. `broadcast test`.
3. Stop recording.
4. Play the demo until the broadcast.
5. Result: The broadcast is logged twice in the local console, indicating that the message was written to the demo twice. In fact, it's written once for every client on the server.

This seems like a general issue with the server's `SendPackMsg` functions:

https://github.com/ddnet/ddnet/blob/6fba46dc84363640d941f9acbf7076069449652f/src/engine/server.h#L83-L114

With client ID `-1`, these call `SendPackMsgOne`/`SendPackMsgTranslate` for each connected client. These then call `SendMsg`, which records the demo unless `MSGFLAG_NORECORD` is set.

Messages intended for all clients should only be recorded to the file once.

title: projectile owner id can match the wrong player on reconnect
body:
Related to https://github.com/ddnet/ddnet/issues/9446 needs ``sv_destroy_bullets_on_death 0`` and ``tune laser_reach 9999999`` to reproduce. The projectile stores ``m_Owner`` which is the non unique regular client id of the owner who shot the projectile. If a player leaves this value is not reset. If a new player joins and the client id gets reused the projectile will change the owner.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/645fc0db-ce37-4b5a-bedb-3126f6a2cde5

Possible fixes are using unique client ids instead of regular client ids. Resetting owner to -1 when a player leaves. Or refactoring the entire code to not make the projectile store the owner at all and store all the information it needs from the owner directly so it can easily out live the owner.

title: Switching from main to dummy discolors tees for 1 tick
`access_level` cannot be separated for subcommands
body:
Currently the ``access_level`` rcon command only supports command names not their sub commands.
So if a admin decides to give helpers access to ``vote no`` but not access to ``vote yes`` that does not work.
The solution for this specific case was the addition of the new rcon command ``vote_no``. A similar thing is done for ``antibot dump`` which can also be called using ``dump_antibot``.

So my proposal would be to add a rcon command that registers aliases instead of manually registering all aliases that might be needed in the code.
Should keep the code base cleaner and the access control more flexible.

A possible autoexec_server.cfg could then look like this

```cfg
# autoexec_server.cfg

add_alias selfkill "kill_pl me"
add_alias kick_antibot "antibot kick"
add_alias tournament "say tournament is starting"
add_alias fastcap "exec fastcap.cfg"

access_level selfkill 1
access_level kick_antibot 1
access_level tournament 1
access_level fastcap 1
```

Idea from: https://github.com/ddnet-insta/ddnet-insta/issues/337

title: sv_destroy_bullets_on_death does not work with ddrace teams
body:
When ``sv_destroy_bullets_on_death`` is ``0`` the flying projectiles have no effect if the owner left the game and was in a ddrace team.
This is caused by the code being a mess.

There is ddrace team code in the character but not in the player. This conceptually sounds very wrong to me. If a player dies their projectiles should still be in that ddrace team. So the player code has to be able to handle that. It works quite well in ddnet because respawning is so fast and joining the spectators kicks you out of the ddrace team.

Similar issues #9229, #9448, #10396, #10398, #10417
Related pending prs #9263, #10399

Imo m_pTeams should be moved from [character.h](https://github.com/ddnet/ddnet/blob/1b5dbe04d95b7375f88b2728749d6ead74b94d0f/src/game/server/entities/character.h#L184) to player.h but the ddrace team information should also be stored on the projectile directly and not depend on the owner still being on the server to get the correct team mask.

All code like this should be removed

https://github.com/ddnet/ddnet/blob/d3dd134bc6bf891f6a0e7cfc22ee1c5d02561c6f/src/game/server/entities/projectile.cpp#L263-L266

Why do we only get the correct team mask if the owner is alive? What if he dies? What if he switches teams? What if he disconnects?

Also gets rid of hacks like this fa3938d7a640257d20452486f421280df251a867 where we need to lock votes for dead players because their team state is lost.

title: Inconsistent Behavior of sv_rescue 1 in team/no-team
body:
I've found an inconsistency when using `sv_rescue 1` and the `/r` command, when playing in a team/no team.

**Steps to Reproduce:**

1. **No Team** / "t0" ([Video Demonstration](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/211c5ba6-c9c2-4b22-9bc7-fe885885c876))
   - No `/r` used: Can finish the map.
   - Use `/r` after start to reset to a position **after** the start line: Can finish the map.
   - Use `/r` after start to reset to a position **before** the start line: Can finish the map.

2. **In Team** ([Video Demonstration](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/51e4ad44-2088-49bf-b385-9c1975389d7f))
   - No `/r` used: Can finish the map.
   - Use `/r` after start to reset to a position **after** the start line: Can finish the map.
   - Use `/r` after start to reset to a position **before** the start line: **Cannot finish the map.**

In the third scenario for both non-team and team case, the timer resets as if the start line was never touched after using `/r` to go back before the start line. In non-team case, re-crossing the start line restarts the timer, allowing the players to finish the map. However, in the team case, the timer does not restart upon re-touching the start line, preventing the team from finishing.

My knowledge about C++ and the ddnet codebase is very limited, so im not sure if im able to fix this myself.

title: Unreproducible Bug: Freeze delayed by 1 Tick
body:
Context
---

Back in November 2023, *Steinchen* shared a clip from the map *Adrenaline 5* in the showroom channel of the DDNet Discord server:

https://github.com/ddnet/ddnet/assets/44099679/4168e50a-7018-4968-8cd3-e8da0b5799d4

[Archived Discussion, also with downloadable demo file](https://archive.strct.cc/ddnet/2023-11-03/bugs.html#chatlog__message-container-1169925381155983430)
It is highly unusual how far the tee was able to go into the freeze wall.
In this small write-up, I'll call the base physics unit (1/32 of a tile) simply *unit*.

- The Tee doesn't touch any other tee
- The Tee's velocity comes entirely from the normal running speed, it does reach the max speed of 10 units per second
- No Hook nor any other special tile is used
- There are no server settings for the map, and no tune zones

Why this should be impossible
---

Every tile is 32 units wide, so to skip a freeze tile, we need to move at least 33 units to land behind the freeze tile. In the video, the tee ends at `.09` in the x coordinate, meaning it moved 3 units further, so at least 36 units through the freeze.

How far a tee can move into a freeze can be calculated quite easily:

- We start at 10 units per second
- The speed always halves with ground friction
- Position changes caused by the velocity are rounded
- The freeze affects the movement only after 1 tick. (This is normal and the reason why you can jump out of freeze, and get frozen at the same time)

| Tick

title: Can trigger teleporters behind other teleporters, even though teleporters are unskippable in general
body:
Dropping tee accumulates vertical speed and after a specific point, it could sometimes trigger outer tele tiles before inner ones.
It is quite an old problem but I do not see any fix or discussion.

Reproducing steps with hammerfly map DDmax-Hell Fly:
This map does not have any checkpoint to limit teleport, purely depends on tele number.
![QQ图片20200203200324](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/32067657/73652005-b3a7b880-46c0-11ea-8455-7bf45d197177.png)
![QQ图片20200203200547](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/32067657/73652052-d76afe80-46c0-11ea-848c-d417d6ff6e73.png)
Falling from the wall along with the arrow(pic1), without any action, tee has a possibility to trigger tele number 4 which is abnormal.
The issue may come from Checking Rate, Tele Tiles Checking Methods.
I am not sure this happens to other tiles.
